classification_basis: reference factory rectangle fitted to one horizontal platform plane; qualify by footprint and perimeter clearance from terrain

small.intent: local or satellite production; limited expansion

medium.intent: dedicated factory with meaningful miner/belt upgrade headroom

large.intent: major production district intended to survive multiple throughput upgrades

very_large.intent: regional or late-game industrial campus where terrain should not be the primary growth constraint

workable.interpretation: placement zone with some directional constraint

poor.interpretation: highly elongated placement zone; rectangle location is more informative than region shape

notes: Every qualifying rectangle is one flat horizontal platform. Its Z is the highest representative terrain cell in that footprint, preventing representative terrain from poking through.

At the working resolution, each cell uses the median of its underlying 1 m terrain samples. This intentionally treats sub-cell rocks/spikes as edge detail rather than allowing one small feature to lift an entire factory platform; decrease the working resolution for a stricter geometric test.

A tolerance of 4 m means both footprint-wide mean clearance and perimeter mean clearance must be <=4 m. Maximum clearance is limited separately to 3x tolerance by default, allowing isolated terrain depressions without treating a broadly grounded platform as floating.

Horizontal sampling resolution and clearance tolerance are independent. Smaller resolution captures more detailed edge conditions; larger clearance tolerance permits more visible foundation exposure/floating.
The irregular region is only the connected zone of rectangle centers that qualify. The emitted rectangles and their fitted platform elevations are the primary planning geometry.
build_surfaces_v4 remains available as the terrain-relief alternative and build_surfaces_v3 as the global elevation-sweep alternative.
